lesson.title: Adding a Directory
lesson.summary: Understand adding a directory from first principles, with a small runnable example.

payload.code:
You can also add and remove directories with add and rm. Let’s say Bob wants to make a
new directory available:

$ mkdir resources
$ touch resources/blah.gif
$ git add resources/
$ git status

# On branch master
# Changes to be committed:
#   (use "git reset HEAD <file>..." to unstage)
#
#       new file: resources/blah.gif
#

payload.markdown: Notice how the contents of resources are added automatically to the repository. Now Bob can commit and then push the whole lot to the remote repository in the usual way.

blocks.text: Notice how the contents of resources are added automatically to the repository. Now Bob can commit and then push the whole lot to the remote repository in the usual way.

payload.text: Note Be careful of using git add with directories; it is greedy! The command will pick up any files and directories beneath the given directory. It is always a good idea to check the operation with git status.
